governing_baseline: G1/action-light; D1; C2; S2; explicit Crossing; Cross/Beat; learned cap 3; Loaded; P1; Counter-first; free before-or-after guard-change harness; Tutta T1
executive_result: Named Guard v0.2 would not presently yield interpretable incentive evidence. Crown C1/B3 has attacker auto-tag and defender reciprocal-motivation failures; repertoire-poor Cross/Beat is a false choice; free guard switching harvests state and access; Alber and Frontale are incentive vacuums; current Nachreisen and Zornhau-Ort behavior is sustained by policy values that exceed their implemented consequences. P1 Power and the C2 compounds retain state-dependent rational uses. Basic Parry is conditionally suppressed at high Skill against known, affordable Durchwechseln but returns with point threat, depletion, or uncertainty.

H1.finding: Crown has the same defence roll/cancellation role as Cross but uniquely grants the attacker Sink Point access and no encoded defender compensation.

H2.finding: B3 Scheitelhau designation adds a future option to an otherwise unchanged Basic Cut and has no cost or downside.

H3.finding: Without Crossing repertoire, active Cross and Beat normally converge after cleanup. Beat is not strictly better because displacement has no persistent active value; the implemented pair is principally a FALSE CHOICE, with possible weak Beat dominance only if separation is valued outside the engine.

H4.finding: Authored Cross continuations create distinct value, but T1 is rational only with exploitable asymmetric Close repertoire; Winden is inactive.

H5.finding: High attacker Skill, high defender Skill, known/affordable D1, and a nonthreatening point can make Basic Parry nearly disappear. Point threat, depletion, low attacker Skill, low defender Skill, and uncertainty restore it.

H6.finding: P1 exchanges fixed 7 damage for 1 Spiritus, Committed restrictions, loss of Durch/insertions, and Counter-first vulnerability. Loaded Cut preserves reserve and continuation access.

H7.finding: T1 is repertoire-dependent. With no owner Close consumer it is an incentive vacuum; with symmetric Pommel access it creates reciprocal risk without owner priority; with owner-only useful Close repertoire it is rational.

H8.finding: Frontale's active mappings are universal Basics and its distinctive learned sequence is inactive.

H9.finding: Free all-to-all switching enables Donna, point-threat, and Play-gate harvesting. The one-change-per-activation timing supplies limited exposure friction but no rules cost.

H10.finding: Cross/Beat mixing, Nachreisen, Crown, T1, guard occupancy, Zornhau-Ort, Pommel frequency, and P1 frequency are materially affected by softmax or hand-authored policy values.

instrumentation_findings: The choices counter records a specific Basic Cross/Beat in defend and then records generic Basic Parry again inside basic_parry; summing choices is invalid.
Crown's dedicated opportunities/declarations/creations and B3 entry declarations are usable; generic plays aggregates do not represent B3 entry declarations and should not be read as such.
Crown ordinary alternatives are not individually instrumented at the Crown decision; an aggregate constant controls branch entry.

The governing baseline records T1, but simulations/shared/provisional_longsword.py selects the Loaded/Power engine and only stores T1 metadata. T1 behavior exists in the separate Guard Play Bridge subclass, not the named-guard engine.
Guard records list Nachreisen access from Vom Tag, but NamedGuardDuel does not enforce that gate. Reported Nachreisen frequency therefore cannot evidence Vom Tag motivation.
Opportunity/use/success/Spiritus/chain/contact metrics are otherwise sufficiently separated for D1, C2, T1, Crown, and guard occupancy when their dedicated fields are used.

ready_answers.A_demonstrably_healthy: Basic Cut/Thrust, Counter/Parry, Ignore/action preservation, P1/Loaded, C2/Basic reserve substitution, and Sink/decline after a valid Crown state.
ready_answers.B_healthy_only_with_repertoire: Generic Cross, T1, Tutta, Pommel, and future Winden identities.
ready_answers.C_strictly_dominated: Crown versus generic Cross/Beat in the candidate; Alber/Frontale versus free point-threat guards in current active mechanics; current Nachreisen and Zornhau-Ort versus their nearest Basic chassis.
ready_answers.D_conditionally_dominated: Basic Parry at expert known/affordable D1; Ochs by Pflug with Absetzen; mapping-only guards by Mezza when their gates are irrelevant; ordinary attack by Pommel in eligible Close states.
ready_answers.E_free_upside: Scheitelhau B3 tagging; before/after guard staging; threatening-point staging when no other gate matters.
ready_answers.F_reciprocal_failures: Scheitelhau/Crown/Sink; current Zornhau-Ort Soft sequence. T1 has reciprocal-risk tension but does not always collapse.
ready_answers.G_guard_vacuums: Alber, Frontale, and current active Vom Tag; Tutta without repertoire. Ochs lacks a fuller active identity but point threat prevents total vacuum.
ready_answers.H_cross_without_repertoire: No distinct rational mechanical reason over Beat in common active states; it is a false choice rather than proven strict Beat dominance.
ready_answers.I_durch_deletes_parry: Materially yes at high Skill, known repertoire, usable reserve, and nonthreatening point; not at low reserve, with threatening point, or under enough uncertainty/poor odds.
ready_answers.J_guard_harvesting: Yes. The behavior is rules-rational; exact churn rates are policy-dependent.
ready_answers.K_policy_artifacts: Cross/Beat frequency, Nachreisen, Crown, T1, Zornhau-Ort, Pommel, guard occupancy, and broad P1 use.
ready_answers.L_severity_3: Crown/entry, Cross/Beat, free switching, Alber/Frontale, point-threat staging comparisons, Nachreisen, and Zornhau-Ort.
ready_answers.M_severity_2_may_wait: expert D1 suppression and Pommel defence denial may wait if explicitly excluded from the v0.2 interpretation; T1 integration/motivation may not.
ready_answers.N_run_now: No. Results would confound missing rules motivation with softmax constants, incomplete repertoire, and free benefit harvesting.
